full_judgment:
8. On behalf of the plaintiff-petitioners it is argued that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division has failed to notice that the presumption of correctness of the entries in the C.S. Khatia.1 under section 103B of the Bengal Tenancy Act had not been rebutted. 

 9. it is no doubt true that an entry in the C.S. Khatian must be presumed to be correct unless the contrary is proved, but when the matter is investigated by the Court on the evidence adduced by the parties on the point in controversy, the entry loses its significance. In the instant case, the lower appellate court, after a detailed discussion of the evidence of the parties came to the conclusion that after the auction sale of the raiyat interest of Salimuddin in 1939 there had been a change in the status and possession of the parties. Therefore the presumption of right, title and possession on the basis of C.S. Khatian did not hold good any more.
